title: HTTP callouts, failures, and bounded retries
summary: Implement a small warranty client and test success, invalid responses, business absence, throttling, server failure, and transport errors locally.
prerequisites: M12 request states and M16 HttpCalloutMock.
learningObjectives: Write a mock that checks the request.
Keep network tests independent of a real server.

sections.heading: Understand the mechanism
body: A callout is a request from Apex to an external HTTP endpoint. Its result has several layers: the transport may fail, the server may return an error status, the body may violate the expected schema, or the body may contain a valid negative business answer. Collapsing all four into 'not covered' would mislead Anna and hide integration failures.

Use a small result contract such as COVERED, NOT_COVERED, NOT_FOUND, RETRYABLE, INVALID_RESPONSE, and TRANSPORT_ERROR. A 429 or selected 5xx response may justify a bounded later retry. A malformed 200 response should be diagnosed as a contract problem. A transport exception does not prove the provider did nothing; for state-changing requests, an unknown remote outcome requires reconciliation rather than a blind retry.

The required tests use HttpCalloutMock. Test.setMock replaces the network response, allowing a deterministic test to assert method, endpoint, and result. The reserved .invalid domain in the example is deliberately not a functioning server. Never run this demo client as a live provider integration. Replace its endpoint with the configured Named Credential only when performing a separately authorized live integration.

Retries belong to orchestration, not an uncontrolled loop around Http.send. Record attempt count, maximum attempts, next eligible time, and the final visible state. In this lesson, implement classification and demonstrate a bounded policy with controlled inputs; do not sleep in a unit test or promise an exact Queueable start time.

callouts.text: A correct retry policy begins by distinguishing failure categories and uncertain outcomes.

sections.heading: Northstar Motors worked example
body: Anna requests a warranty check. A 200 body containing covered=false is a successful negative answer. A 404 means the fictional provider has no matching vehicle. A 500 means the request did not yield a usable answer and may be retried under policy. The sample below is a complete minimal client class for the local mock exercise; it is not the complete request orchestration or production integration.

Create a separate test class implementing HttpCalloutMock. Its respond method should assert GET and the expected VIN in the endpoint, then return controlled status/body pairs. Register a different mock for each case and assert the returned classification. Include a mock that throws CalloutException and one with an invalid covered type.

callouts.text: Which result states mean a business answer was obtained, rather than merely an HTTP response?

codeBlocks.caption: Complete minimal WarrantyDemoClient.cls; test-only endpoint, no real server

sections.heading: Build and inspect
body: Save the complete client in your own training DX project with matching Apex metadata. The mock class and test methods are your guided task. No Named Credential is required for the mock-only endpoint; do not make a live request.

When the M12 worker makes HTTP calls, declare implements Queueable, Database.AllowsCallouts. Read the request first, perform the callout before pending DML, then save the result and attempt history. Updating Processing or inserting a log before Http.send in that same transaction can cause an uncommitted-work error. A prior entry transaction may persist Queued and enqueue the worker; it commits separately. For multiple requests, design callout/write ordering deliberately rather than alternating a call and DML in a loop. The durable claim/concurrency policy remains a separate orchestration responsibility.

steps.title: Build the response mock
steps.instruction: Implement HttpCalloutMock with constructor values for status and body. Assert the expected request method and synthetic VIN inside respond.
steps.expected: The test fails if the client sends the wrong request.

steps.title: Test all classifications
steps.instruction: Register mocks for covered true/false with a valid expiresOn string, 404, 429, 500, malformed JSON, missing fields, wrong Boolean type, invalid or missing expiry date, and a transport exception. Assert INVALID_RESPONSE for bodies that violate either required field.
steps.expected: Every response produces the declared safe result.

steps.title: Connect the bounded policy
steps.instruction: Map the classifications to M12 request states and an attempt limit. Demonstrate two transient attempts followed by success with controlled responses, then exhaustion.
steps.expected: A retry never silently becomes a completed warranty decision.

sections.heading: Failure cases and boundaries
body: A test that returns 200 for every request can pass even when the endpoint or HTTP method is wrong. Assert the outgoing contract.
The catch for body parsing must not hide a successful business response under an unrelated status. Keep classification tests focused enough to identify the incorrect branch.

callouts.text: Do not log Authorization headers, credentials, or unrestricted response payloads when diagnosing failures.

exercise.title: Test the warranty client locally
exercise.brief: Implement the mock and bounded orchestration mapping around the supplied client.
steps: Record the retry limit and final user-visible state.
acceptance: All tests run without a provider.
A valid negative answer differs from failure.
Retry exhaustion is visible and does not loop indefinitely.
exercise.stretch: Explain one limitation and propose a small follow-up experiment before extending the implementation.

knowledgeCheck.question: Is covered=false an error?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Under this contract it is a valid business result.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does a transport exception prove?
knowledgeCheck.answer: That the caller did not obtain a usable response; it does not universally prove the remote side performed no action.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why assert the request in the mock?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Otherwise a wrong URL, method, or input could receive a fake success and pass unnoticed.

recap: Separate transport, protocol, schema, and business outcomes.
Mock the outgoing contract as well as the response.
